quick: 5-30 mL/day IV/IM (parenteral); oral forms vary by product
No specific data; avoid heavy use
summary: Cerebroprotein hydrolysate (Cerebrolysin) is a peptide preparation derived from purified porcine brain proteins, marketed in parts of Europe and Asia for stroke, dementia and traumatic brain injury. It is NOT FDA-approved and evidence of clinical benefit is limited and contested. Doses follow manufacturer SmPC; this record reflects EMA-region/SmPC and BNF-type sources rather than an FDA label.
indications: Adjunctive treatment in ischemic stroke (per regional approvals)
Dementia of Alzheimer's type and vascular dementia (per regional approvals)
Sequelae of traumatic brain injury / cerebral trauma
Note: indications vary by country; NOT FDA-approved for any use

dosage.d: Up to 30-50 mL/day by slow IV infusion for 10-21 days
dosage.n: Per SmPC; dilute and infuse slowly

admin: Administer by slow IV infusion (dilute in compatible solution) or IM injection per product
Doses up to 10 mL may be given by slow IV injection; larger volumes by infusion
Inspect solution; do not mix with amino-acid-incompatible or alkaline solutions
Give as defined treatment courses rather than indefinitely
moa: Proposed to exert neurotrophic and neuroprotective effects mimicking endogenous neurotrophic factors. The low-molecular-weight peptide fraction is thought to modulate neuronal metabolism, reduce excitotoxicity and oxidative damage, and support neuronal survival and synaptic plasticity. The precise mechanism is not fully established.

absolute: Status epilepticus or active epileptic seizures
monitor: Patients with epilepsy or seizure history
Signs of allergic reaction during infusion

preg: Limited data; avoid during pregnancy unless clearly necessary and the potential benefit outweighs risk.
lact: Limited data; avoid during breastfeeding or discontinue nursing.
renal: Contraindicated/avoid in severe renal impairment; use caution in lesser degrees of impairment.
hepatic: Specific hepatic dosing not defined; use clinical judgment.

moderate: MAO inhibitors and antidepressants - theoretical additive effects; use with caution
interactions.alcohol: No specific data; avoid heavy alcohol use.

common: Sensation of heat/flushing (especially with rapid infusion)

monitoring: Clinical and neurological response over the treatment course
counsel: This is given as a course of injections/infusions, not a daily pill for life
Tell staff if you feel hot, flushed or dizzy during the infusion
Report any history of seizures or allergies before treatment
Be aware that evidence for benefit is limited and it is not approved in all countries
pk: Not formally established for the peptide fraction
Store per product label, protect from light; do not freeze
pearls: NOT FDA-approved; used in EU/Asia (SmPC/BNF-type sourcing) - clinical evidence is limited and debated
Derived from purified porcine brain proteins
Give slowly; rapid infusion causes flushing/heat sensation
Avoid in severe renal impairment and active epilepsy
missed: As this is given as supervised injection/infusion courses, a missed dose should be managed by the treating clinician; do not attempt to self-administer extra doses.
overdose: No specific antidote. Overdose may intensify adverse effects (e.g., dizziness, agitation, hypersensitivity). Discontinue and provide symptomatic and supportive care.
